rows.question: How does the AVAPrintDB benchmark produce one verification score for two avatar videos of different lengths?
expected_answer_points: Each video is split into fixed-length windows with stride F/2, each window is embedded, cosine similarities between all enrollment and test windows are computed, and the score is their average.

rows.question: How does InstructAvatar feed emotion instructions and facial-motion instructions into its generator differently?
expected_answer_points: Two cross-attention branches: the emotion branch uses the CLIP [EOS] token as a global style signal, while the motion branch uses all last-layer CLIP token states for time-varying detail, each with its own adapter.
rows.answer: InstructAvatar feeds emotion instructions through a single [EOS] token from the CLIP text encoder, which provides overall style guidance throughout the video, while facial-motion instructions use the hidden states of all tokens from the last layer of CLIP to capture dynamic, time-varying actions [S1]. The emotion branch uses a fixed [EOS] token for consistent emotional control, whereas the motion branch leverages detailed temporal information via full token hidden states [S1]. To align the two instruction spaces with the diffusion model, different adapters (Ae, Am) are introduced for emotion and motion branches respectively [S1]. The two branches are processed in parallel within the denoising blocks, with cross-attention mechanisms enabling text injection into the latent space [S1].

rows.question: Why does MotionDiffuse replace standard self-attention in its motion decoder?
expected_answer_points: Standard attention is quadratic in sequence length and motions can be hundreds of frames, so it uses Efficient Attention (linear), whose global feature map also aggregates useful global context.
rows.answer: MotionDiffuse replaces standard self-attention with cross-attention to inject text features into the motion sequence generation process, enabling text-conditioned motion synthesis [S1]. This modification allows the model to explicitly fuse text information with motion features during denoising steps, improving control and diversity in motion generation [S1]. The cross-attention mechanism replaces the key and value matrices in self-attention with those derived from text features, ensuring the motion sequence is guided by textual descriptions [S1]. This design supports more flexible and semantically meaningful motion generation compared to standard self-attention [S1].

rows.question: Why does Real3D-Portrait's image-to-plane network have both a ViT branch and a VGG branch?
expected_answer_points: The ViT (SegFormer) branch handles pixel-to-world canonicalization via attention, but patch embedding loses high-frequency texture, so a normalization-free VGG convolution branch extracts high-frequency appearance.
rows.answer: The image-to-plane (I2P) network includes both a ViT branch and a VGG branch to jointly handle 3D reconstruction and appearance fidelity: the ViT branch performs efficient pixel-to-world coordinate transformation and captures global structural features via attention, while the VGG branch extracts high-frequency texture details through convolutional layers to preserve fine appearance details in the rendered face [S1]. The two branches are fused to combine global structure and local texture, ensuring both accurate 3D reconstruction and visual fidelity [S1].
